title: Realistic Knitwear Designer
content: **Create realistic knitwear with a variety of stitches.** [![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59706892372889) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/A_fkc7n4fzU?si=tYrcktcrKHn6kjA-) ### 1. Click the Fabric in the Fabric tab in the Object Browser, and then change the Material Type to Knitwear in the Property Editor. 2. Adjust each detail property to express the desired knitwear. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Stitching** | Set the knit's Stitching type. **Yarn Thickness** | Set the thickness of the yarn. **Gauge** | Gauge refers to the number of knitting stitches within an inch. This means you can control the size of a stitch in the knit fabric: Higher values represent denser, thinner knits, and lower values represent thicker knits. **Transformation** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59665160530201) | **Knit Direction** | Adjust the Knit Direction independently. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59665160531737)Link to Pattern's Grain Direction** | Link Knit Direction to the pattern's [Grain Direction](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/37494551581593-Grainline). When linked, Knit Direction is driven by the Grain Direction. When unlinked, Knit Direction works independently which unaffected by the Grain Direction. **Position X** | Adjust the horizontal position of the knit structure. **Position Y** | Adjust the vertical position of the knit structure. **Ply Amount** | Set the number of threads for plying. **Ply Randomization** **(Melange)** | Plying is randomly blended to create a natural melange effect. **Randomization Factor** | Adjust the density of the plying. Higher values result in a denser appearance. **Seed Position** | Adjust the position of the plying. **Yarn Variance** | **Irreqularity** | **Scale** | Adjust how much the yarn randomly moves. **Frequency** | Adjust how often the yarn direction changes. **Slub** **(Pilling)** | **Length (mm)** | Adjust how short or long the fluff can get. Higher values result in a longer slub appearance. **Thickness** | Adjust how thick the fluff can get. Higher values result in a thicker slub appearance. **Frequency** | Adjust how often the fluff appears. **Generate Seams** | Additional yarn is created along the seam lines and pattern outlines. If the seams in the knitwear pattern look unnatural, adjust the option to make them look more natural. **Ply Normal Map** | Apply the normal map to the plying to express the three-dimensional effect of the yarn. **Ply Color** | Set the color for each yarn in the plying. **📝 Note:** * It may affect performance and speed when applying knitwear, and you can turn off the **![Garment Surface Textured Thick Normal.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29738213752217)****Garment Rendering Style** in 3D window ▶ ![Garment Option Kintwear Mesh.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29738213766041)**Show Knitwear** during other operations to work at the same speed as before. * To optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image, apply the settings in [Render Properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties) ▶ Mesh Optimization.
content_description: "Discover how to create realistic knitwear by mastering various stitch types and adjusting essential fabric properties for your designs."

title: Simulation
content: Use this function to apply gravity and drape 3D garments in the 3D Window. Clicking on the simulate button causes all pattern pieces to fall towards the floor and drape onto avatars and similar (static collision) objects that are in the way. When seamlines are set between pattern pieces, the fabric drapes and falls while the set seamlines are sewn. # **Location** **3D Toolbar ▶** **CPU: Normal (Default)![CPU: Normal \(Default\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856321214489)** **CPU: Fitting (Accurate Fabric)![CPU: Fitting \(Accurate Fabric\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856382868249)** **CPU: Animation (Stable)![CPU: Animation \(Stable\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856321215001)** **GPU: Normal (Default)![GPU: Normal \(Default\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856321215129)** **GPU: Fitting (Accurate Fabric)![GPU: Fitting \(Accurate Fabric\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856382868889)** **GPU: Animation (Stable)![GPU: Animation \(Stable\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53856382869017)** Click and hold the tool to change in between the simulation options in the appearing pop-up window. * * * **Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ Simulate** # **Simulation Modes** **![CPU: Normal \(Default\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065410464793)![GPU: Normal \(Default\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065410471193)****Normal (Default):** Garment simulation is more efficient with faster speed. **![CPU: Fitting \(Accurate Fabric\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065410467993)![GPU: Fitting \(Accurate Fabric\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065387979161)****Fitting (Accurate Fabric):** Garment simulation is more defined and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically. **![CPU: Animation \(Stable\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065387971609)![GPU: Animation \(Stable\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065410472729)****Animation (Stable):** Garment simulation is more defined but the simulation speed may decrease. # **CPU or GPU?** Switch between how collision is calculated - via processor or graphic card unit. GPU has the same level of accuracy and collision handling as CPU simulation in all modes. For trims, collision and weight only work with CPU simulation.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the gravity simulation function to accurately drape 3D garments in the 3D Window, allowing users to visualize fabric behavior on avatars and objects.

title: Punch Mark Tool
content: **New in 2026.0** Create Punch Mark Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Convert to Button Head / Button Hole Grading Export / Import Place drill hole markers on a pattern piece in the 2D window to indicate exact punch locations for cutting machines. #### **Create Punch Mark** 1. Click the **Punch Mark![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59489838689433)** in the 2D toolbar. * **** The Punch Mark tool is grouped under the Notch tool in the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click on the desired location on the 2D Pattern. → A Punch Mark is placed at that point. **📝****Note:** Right-click on the pattern to input exact X and Y placement values. #### **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** Unlike internal shapes, Punch Marks are not automatically mirrored to the symmetric pattern. To duplicate: 1. Select the Punch Mark(s). 2. Right-click and select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. → The Punch Mark(s) are added to the symmetric pattern independently and can be moved or deleted without affecting the original. #### **Convert to Button Head / Button Hole** 1. Select the Punch Mark(s). 2. Right-click and select Convert to Button Head or Convert to Button Hole. → The Punch Mark is replaced with the corresponding button object at the same position. #### **Grading** Adjust the position of a Punch Mark per grade size. 1. Create or apply grading sizes to the pattern. 2. Select the Punch Mark using the Grading tool in the 2D Toolbar. 3. Use the arrow keys or enter values directly to set the position offset for each size. → The Punch Mark shifts position per grade while the diameter remains unchanged. **📝****Note:****** Grading rules only affect Punch Mark placement, not size. Grading offsets are preserved when exporting to DXF. #### **Export / Import** * **DXF Export / Import** **Export:** Punch Marks export to **Layer 13 (DXF_DRILL_HOLE)** , the industry-standard layer that cutting machines recognize as drill instructions. Grading values are preserved. **Import:** Punch Marks on DXF Layer 13 are imported automatically — no additional settings required. * **Export Plotter (PLT)** Punch Marks appear under **Line Options** in the PLT export dialog, enabled by default. The pen assignment can be set independently. * **2D Snapshot / PDF / Print Layout** Punch Marks are rendered using the Punch Mark symbol, consistent with their appearance in the 2D window.
content_description: Discover the powerful new features in version 2026.0, including Punch Mark creation, symmetry duplication, button conversion, grading adjustments, and seamless DXF export/import to enhance your pattern design workflow.

title: Pattern Annotation
content: #### **List of Contents** Create Edit Link Annotation to Line Show/Hide #### Set the orientation, size, and color of pattern annotations for quick and clear access to pattern information. #### #### **Create** 1. Click 2D toolbar ▶ ![Pattern Annotation On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512372632217) **Pattern Annotation** tool. 2. Click the Pattern to add an annotation, then press **Ctrl + Enter** on the keyboard or click anywhere else to complete. #### #### **Edit** 1. Click 2D toolbar ▶ ![Edit Annotation On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512372633625)**Edit Annotation** tool. 2. Move the added annotation by clicking and dragging, or rotate it by clicking and dragging the pivot point in the desired direction. 3. Click the annotation, then set the properties in the Property Editor. **Property** | **Description** ---|--- **Orientation** | Set the orientation of the annotation. **Font Size** | Adjust the font size of the annotation. **Color** | Change the color of the annotation. 4. Right-click the annotation to set options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected annotation. **Copy & Paste** | Copy the annotation and paste it at the desired position **Rotate** | Rotate the annotation in the desired direction. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512351583769)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568923053081) **Pattern Names** on 2D Patterns can now be selected and edited using the **Edit Annotation** tool. To edit an annotation or pattern name, either double-click the text directly or select it in the 2D window and update the content using the **Text** field in the Property Editor. #### #### **Link Annotation to Line/Point** Link Pattern Annotations to specific Pattern Outlines/points or Internal Lines/points to maintain their relative position when patterns are modified. 1. Select the **Edit Annotation** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the annotation in the 2D window, and select **Link to**. 3. Click on the **Pattern Outline** or**Internal Line** to be linked. → The annotation anchors to the line, and a dashed connection line appears. 4. To remove the link, right-click the annotation and select **Unlink**. **📝 Note:** * **Automatic Movement:** Linked annotations automatically follow the movement and transformation of their parent line. * **Connection Visibility:** The dashed link indicator is only visible when the annotation is selected or when the Annotation tool is active. #### **Show/Hide** 1. Click ![Info Main Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512351587225) Information Display ▶ ![Info Sub Annotation Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512372650265) **Show Annotation** in 2D window to show or hide pattern annotations as needed. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating, editing, linking, and managing pattern annotations in a 2D design environment for enhanced clarity and organization of pattern information.

title: Pinching Simulation Override
content: # **New in 2026.1** **** Temporarily overrides global and fabric simulation properties during pinching. **** ## **Location** To enable Pinching Simulation Override dialog: 1. In the 3D window, use the mouse to right-click an empty area, then select Simulation Properties. Alternatively, go to Settings > Preferences > Simulation Properties. 2. Enable the Pinching Simulation Override checkbox. When Pinching Simulation Override is enabled, the Pinching Simulation Override dialog appears whenever a Pinching tool is activated in Simulation mode. ## **** ## **Operation** ### **Rest Shape** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Update Rest Shape** | Updates the Rest Shape using the current 3D state. **Reset Rest Shape** | Restores the Rest Shape to its original pattern-based state. **Selected Patterns / All Patterns** | Sets the scope to which the Rest Shape update or reset is applied. **Show Rest Shape Override** | Displays patterns with changed Rest Shapes in gray in the 3D window. ### **Simulation Properties** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Override Strength** | Sets how much Pinching Simulation Override is applied. 0 uses the original simulation properties, and 1 fully applies the override properties. **Global** | Adjusts the global simulation properties used when the override is fully applied. **Fabric** | Adjusts the fabric simulation properties used when the override is fully applied. The fabrics to override can be selected using checkboxes. ## **** ## **Notes** * Update Rest Shape changes the reference shape that the simulation restores toward, helping maintain the edited shape during pinching. * Updating the Rest Shape causes the result to differ from the original pattern-based shape and area. Repeated updates can increase this difference. * Pinching Simulation Override is designed to support editing the base garment shape through pinching, not simulations driven by moving collision objects. * To maintain the edited shape in Animation Record, apply Solidify after pinching.
content_description: Explore the new Pinching Simulation Override feature in 2026.1, allowing you to temporarily adjust global and fabric simulation properties for enhanced garment shape editing during pinching.

title: Can I use my own accessories (hair, shoes, etc.) for CLO Avatars?
content: **Question** Can I use my own accessories (hair, shoes, etc.) for CLO Avatars? **Answer** You may import personal accessories into CLO as OBJ, FBX and other 3D file types, but they won't be automatically placed where the Avatar's hair or shoes is. To use personal accessories as CLO's hair and shoes, some advanced configuration need to be made in other 3D tools such as Maya. If you would like to use accessories other than default items, please check out [CLO-SET CONNECT](https://connect.clo-set.com/).
content_description: Explore how to customize your CLO Avatars with personal accessories by importing 3D files and learn about advanced configuration options for optimal placement.

title: Flatten
content: **Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar.** **** **📝****Note:** * The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. * Since version 2024.2, the 2D pattern position and rotation are more aligned with the pattern placement on the 3D avatar. It is recommended to use CLO avatar for extracting the ideal pattern with front and back positions in the 2D window. When using a non-CLO avatar (eg. FBX) or missing the avatar, it is possible to lead to a non-ideal pattern position in the 2D window. #### 1. In the 3D toolbar, press and hold the **![3D Pen Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55637066431513)3D Pen (Avatar)** and switch to the ![Flatten On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49948392732569) **Flatten.** **** 2. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as Pattern. 3. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. 4. Press**Enter** on the keyboard. → The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. → Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. 5. Hold down **Shift** and press **Enter.** → The intersecting area is flattened into a single pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a guide for extracting closed shapes as patterns from an Avatar, ensuring optimal alignment between 2D and 3D views for accurate pattern placement.

title: [Print Layout Mode] Roll Width
content: **List of Contents** Roll Width Roll Width Properties Margins ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569593512857) **Roll Width** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P_WA3drM340 \- Adjust the width of the fabric roll in the Print Layout Mode. \- Main Menu ▶ Simulation Mode Button ▶ **PRINT LAYOUT**. **Roll Width Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T1uAioXc-BA \- Select the **Edit Texture** tool from the 3D toolbar. Then, select the Pattern with a texture to be edited. → The selected texture's properties appear in the Property Editor. \- Adjust **Width** and **Position** under the **Roll** option (ver5.0.0.) \- For **Width** , select a preset from the drop-down menu on the right, or insert specific values to either the **in** or **mm** option. \- Change the fabric placement with the **Position** option (ver5.0.0.) → The fabric placement changes based on the inserted values. #### **Margins** \- Set the boundary margins of the fabric roll under the **Margins** option in the Property Editor.![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569593514777) \- Adjust **Side A** and **Side B** under **Selvedge Margin** to set the left and right margins along the fabric width. \- Adjust **Start** and **End** under **Cut-Line Margin** to set the top and bottom margins along the fabric length. → The fabric boundary updates based on the entered values. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Print Layout Display
content: **Objective** Show or hide information such as texture repeat grid, pattern names or baselines in the Print Layout Mode. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ **PRINT LAYOUT** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Right-click and set the following options in the 2D window. **Texture Repeat Grid** | Repeat grid of the texture displays. ---|--- **Snap to Texture Grid** | Outline | The pattern piece is snapped to the outline of the texture. Center (ver 6.1) | The pattern piece is snapped to the center of the texture. **Snap to Pattern** | The pattern piece is snapped to another piece. **Zoom Extents All** | 2D Pattern Window zooms out to display all patterns. You can hide or show the [line ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360011148874-2D-%EC%B0%BD-%EB%82%B4-%EB%B3%B4%EA%B8%B0-%EC%95%84%EC%9D%B4%EC%BD%98#Click2)or [information](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360011148874-2D-%EC%B0%BD-%EB%82%B4-%EB%B3%B4%EA%B8%B0-%EC%95%84%EC%9D%B4%EC%BD%98#Click3) of 2D patterns at the top-left corner. **※Note:** If you do not have access to a plotter and are looking for a way to print with a standard-sized printer, please find this tutorial on the CLO YouTube channel: YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7el2V_d5tmQ **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569378411161)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569388567577) #### **Marker Direction** Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59533164852889) **Rotate** button at the bottom-right corner to switch the marker orientation between **Vertical** and **Horizontal**. → In **Vertical** mode, Width runs along the X-axis and Length along the Y-axis. → In **Horizontal** mode, the axes are swapped. → Pattern placement and grainline alignment are preserved during the switch.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to toggle the visibility of various elements in Print Layout Mode, allowing users to manage texture repeat grids, pattern names, and baselines effectively.

title: 2D Snapshot (1:1)
content: **Objective** Save real size 2D pattern (1:1). **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Patterns (1:1)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Patterns (1:1)** → 2D window is enlarged, 2D Snapshot window appears. 2. Set the file format, snapshot size, and other options. 📝 Note: When selecting the file format, the provided options will be different. **Options** --- **File Format** | ![2025.2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59531040441241) Set the File Format for your Print Layout 2D snapshot. The following formats are supported: PDF / PNG / JPEG / DXF - Standard / DXF - AAMA / DXF - ASTM **Preset** | Select the snapshot image size. **Orientation** | Select the paper orientation. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Set the unit of the print paper. **Resolution** | Set the resolution of the snapshot image. **Scale** | Set the scale of the image. **Rotation** | Set whether to rotate the file and the rotation direction. **Line Options** | Select the line and style that appear in the 2D window. **Add'l Information** | Select the information that appears in the 2D window. **Show Images** | **Pattern Texture** | View or hide the pattern texture. **Graphic** | View or hide the graphic. 3. Click **Save** , then enter a filename and select the desired save path. → 2D Patterns(1:1) is saved. **📝****Note:** In 2026.0 or older versions, click **Save,** then enter a filename and select the desired save path and set the Scale and Rotation, click **OK** to save the file.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for saving a real-size 2D pattern snapshot (1:1) in various file formats, allowing users to customize their output settings before finalizing the save process.

title: Express Cartoon
content: ### **New in 2026.0** **** This feature allows for a unique cartoon-style look using fabric and avatar materials. #### **Workflow** 1. Select a fabric style or an avatar. 2. In the Property Editor, set Material ▶ Type ▶**Toon (Viewport Only)**. 3. Adjust the displayed property values to achieve your desired style. #### #### **Options** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Base Color** | **Color** | Corresponds to MToon’s Lit Color parameter, representing the original color visible when receiving 100% light. **Base Color Map** | The texture map used for the Base Color **Opacity** | **Color** | Transparency settings for the Base Color. The overall transparency value. **Opacity Map** | Apply Common UI for assigning Texture Maps / Adding Maps. **Shade** | **Color** | The RGB color of the shadow. **Shade Color Map** | A texture applied specifically to shadow areas. Often uses the same texture as the Base Color or is left empty. **Hardness** | The degree of sharpness of the shadow edges. **Shift** | Adjusts the threshold where shadows begin to form. Higher values result in larger shadow areas. **Emission** | **Color** | Configures the parts that glow self-luminously, unaffected by external lighting. The color that glows brightly even in dark environments. **Emission Map** | The texture map used for parts that glow in the dark. **MatCap** | **Color** | MatCap is a fake refelction effect. The color to be blended with the MatCap image. **Matcap Map** | A texture that stores pre-captured ambient lighting information, layering a glossy effect on the surface based on the camera's viewing angle. **Rim Light** | **Color** | Rim Light(Halo) effect formed on the inner edges of the character. **Fresnel Power** | Adjusts the thickness and sharpness of the rim light. Controls the falloff of the light-affected area. **Lift** | Adjusts the position offset of the rim light. **Outline** | **Mode** | Creates a border line to achieve a cartoon-like aesthetic. Mode is the method of generating the outline. **Outline Map** | A texture used for masking to prevent outlines from appearing on specific areas. **Color** | The color of the line. **Width (mm)** | The thickness of the line. **📝****Note:** The Toon type is only visible in the Viewport and will not be applied to V-ray render.
content_description: Explore the new cartoon-style feature in version 2026.0, designed to enhance your avatars and fabrics with customizable materials for a vibrant, playful look.

title: UV Editor
content: **List of Contents** **Open UV Editor** **Move UV** **Auto UV Packing** **UV Options** **Bake Textures** **UV Snapshot** **UV Display** **** Create UV maps of patterns, buttons, zippers and more to bake normal, roughness, metalness, and alpha maps. U is the horizontal axis and V is the vertical axis in the graph. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45595894327961) [Watch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gt-YmEutZbk) #### **Open UV Editor** 1. Select Materials/UV ▶ **UV Editor** in the top menu. 2. Click the Map icon at the top-left corner of the UV Editor to switch to a different PBR map. #### **** #### **Move UV** 1. Click **Move UV** tool. 2. Set the moving distance. Distance 1 indicates the length of the segment of the UV Tile in the UV Editor. 3. Move the UV by clicking the arrow icon or pressing the directional keys on the keyboard. → UV is moved according to the distance you set. 4. Or click a pattern and drag to move its UVs. #### **** #### **Auto UV Packing** 1. Click**Auto UV Packing** tool. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25701576108569) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=9IysllLmqtyUXtAV&t=4306) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Option** | **Padding** | Sets the spacing between UVs. Values ​​are applied in a fraction of the UV tile size. (0.001 ~ 0.999) **Fidelity** | Adjust UV accuracy from 1 to 5. The higher the value, the more accurate the placement is as it is calculated in the original form, but as the amount of calculation increases, it takes more time. **Fix Scale Ratio** | Fix the size ratio of UVs. **Advanced Placement** | It is calculated in a more advanced way and is placed with optimal results with minimal empty space, but the larger the number of patterns, the more time it takes. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Set to default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Set by directly entering UV coordinates. #### **UV Options** 1. Right-click on the desired pattern. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Select** | **All with Same Property** | All Patterns with the same particle distance, Layer and Fabric will be selected. **Select All Sewn** | Selects all patterns sewn to the initially selected pattern. 2. Or right-click on the background. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Arrange with UV** **(0-1)** | Fit All UV to 0-1. **Length (Absolute)** | Enter the actual distance value from the outline to offset the distance. **UV Coordinate (Relative)** | Enter a value between 0-1 from the outline to offset the distance. **Reset UV to 2D Arrangement** | Reset all UV to 2D Arrangements. #### #### **UV Bake Textures** 1. Click **Bake Textures** tool. 2. After setting the following options, click **Save**. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **Saving Path** | Specify the saving path and the format (PNG / JPEG / PDF) for baked textures. **Size (Pixels)** | Set the size of the image. The image is saved as a square. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Save the default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Save 1 selected tile. If users enter the UV coordinates to be saved, only one tile is saved. **All Tiles** | Save all tiles. **Fill Texture Seams** | The texture fills outside the seamline by the entered value in pixels. **Infinite Seams** | Fill the seamline to the entire area outside of the pattern. **Texture Type** | Select the type of texture to bake. #### **UV Snapshot** 1. Click **UV Snapshot** tool. 2. After setting the following options, click **Save**. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **Saving Path** | Specifies the storage path for UV Snapshot. **Size (Pixels)** | Set the size of the image. The image is saved as a square and if the option "Anti-alias Lines" is checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segment. **Edge Color** | Set the color of the wire segment. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Save the default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Save 1 selected tile. If users enter the UV coordinates to be saved, only one tile is saved. **All Tiles** | Save all tiles. ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55501783845017) #### **UV Display** 1. Click the **UV Display** icon in the UV Editor. → Icons for UV display methods will appear. 2. Refer to the following to select the UV display target. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **UV Display Target** | **Show All Objects** | Displays the UVs of all garments and avatars in the scene. **Show Selected Objects** | Displays only the UVs of the selected garments and avatars. **📝****Note:** The UV Display Element cannot be controlled when this option is activated. **UV Display Element** | **Show Garment** | Displays the UVs of garments. **Show Avatar** | Displays the UVs of avatars.
content_description: Discover essential tools and features for creating, managing, and optimizing UV maps to enhance your 3D modeling and texturing workflow.

title: Auto 3D Arrangement (ver 7.1)
content: **Objective** Automatically arrange patterns around the Avatar in the 3D window. Based on the results learned from a number of pattern data, Auto 3D Arrangement analyzes where the pattern will be arranged only with the shape of the pattern. It is recommended to apply symmetry and sewing before Auto 3D Arrangement, as symmetry and sewing information of patterns as well as shapes are referenced for more accurate arrangement. **Location**** ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Auto 3D Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Auto 3D Arrangement** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → Auto 3D Arrangement Window appears. 2. Click the Proceed button. → Patterns with high accuracy are arranged in order, and the patterns arranged in each step are classified by color and transparency. 3. If you want to check the arrangement result of each step, Click the Back and Next buttons. → Return to the Back and Next Steps. 4. Click the OK button to complete the Auto 3D Arrangement. ※Note: Patterns that are too small in size or analyzed in the same location may not be automatically arranged with lower accuracy.
content_description: This web page provides a streamlined guide for using the Auto 3D Arrangement tool to automatically organize garment patterns around an Avatar in a 3D environment, enhancing design accuracy through symmetry and sewing considerations.

title: Sew Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Sew Patterns and Block Boxes Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing ### **Objective** Set seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. **Location** Library Menu ▶ **MODULAR LIBRARY** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59328521114521) **Operation** **Sew Patterns and Block Boxes** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2. Click on**![Segment Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021281305) Segment sewing **tool or ![Free Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165036872089) **Free sewing** tool. 3. Set seamlines for Pattern and its relative Block Boxes (Step 2 and 3 do not necessarily need to be in order). 4. Set Pattern outlines (Patterns must be sewn one another i.e. shoulder seams, armholes, side seams) and seamlines between Block Boxes. 5. Repeat the steps above for the remains. **※ Note:** * Block Boxes can only be sewn with **Segment Sewing**. In other words, sewing multiple Block Box segments at once by using **M:N Free Sewing** is not allowed. Therefore if the number of Block Box segments is higher than the number of segments need to be sewn, add segments on the patterns to make the number equal, then sew them 1:1. ex) In case of a basic t-shirt block, there is a point added on the neck segment. Therefore add a point on its pattern, then sew the segments 1:1. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Pattern and the Block Boxes has no effect on the simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. **Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 2. 2D Toolbar default presets ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing** tool. → While the tool is toggled on, it enables to check the seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. 3. Deselect ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show modular sewing** / **Show pattern sewing** tool. → Block Boxes to Pattern seamlines disappears but for Patterns to Patterns are appeared. **※ Note:** If seamlines do not appear after setting Pattern and Block Boxes, please confirm ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing** toggle status. **Note: If your modular library appears empty and the default assets are missing, please ensure that CLO has been granted full disk access permissions in your computer's system settings.** Please see the following article for step-by-step instructions on this process: [Disk access rights required when CLO is running](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697-Disk-access-rights-required-when-CLO-is-running) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for setting seamlines between patterns and block boxes in modular sewing, ensuring accurate and efficient garment construction.

title: Zipper
content: **List of Contents** Zipper Creating Zipper Unzip/Zip Zipper Edit Zipper Tape/ Slider Property Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu **Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1wDMdx1Fa-g \- Create and express zippers easily and quickly. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** ****Creating Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hc-HRRg4IGk \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- The Pattern outlines and Internal Lines on the 3D Garment will appear as dashed lines. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the Zipper will be placed. \- Click once and drag the mouse cursor along the Pattern outline or Internal Line. \- Double click to complete the first half of the Zipper. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the other half of the Zipper will be placed. \- Repeat the same procedure. A blue dot will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Zipper. \- When the Zipper is established, the Zipper tape and the Zipper slider will appear along the designated Pattern outlines or Internal Lines. \- The Zipper slider will always be located at the starting position where Zipper was placed \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D Toolbar. \- The Zipper will fasten. **Unzip/ Zip Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLlU1vC6pcE \- With Simulation off, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to partially unzip or Zip the Zipper. \- Click on the Zipper slider, and it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Click and drag the Zipper slider along the Zipper tape. A grey slider will follow along the mouse to preview the location. \- Release the mouse to finalize Zipper slider’s location. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D toolbar. \- Only the designated part of the Zipper will fasten or unfasten. **Editing Zipper Tape/ Slider Property** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2DpM0NKENC8 \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to select either the Zipper tape or the Zipper slider. * **Zipper Tape YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eBunmqATU0E ** * **Width (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign width to the Zipper tape. ** ** * **Thickness (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign thickness to the Zipper tape. \- Change the Garment Rendering Style to ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022824148/mceclip4.png) **Thick Textured Surface** to see Zipper tape’s thickness. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Toggle on/off the option to completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle Off the **Fasten Zipper** option to unzip the zipper. * **Material - Texture** \- Change the texture of the Zipper tape. \- Add Normal Map and check on/off **Desaturation** to convert the texture into greyscale. * **Material - Color** \- Change the color of the Zipper tape. \- Adjust **Ambient Intensity** and **Diffuse Intensity** as needed. **Ambient Intensity** expresses the effect of ambient light. **Diffuse Intensity** controls the intensity of the applied texture image and color. \- Adjust **Specular Colo** r as needed. With the **Shininess** option, modify the sheen of the Zipper tape. \- Add Specular Map to assign how **Specular Color** is applied to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust **Emission Color** to set the color that emits from the Zipper tape. * **Fold** -**Strength:** set the strength of the fold of the Sewing Line between the Pattern and the Zipper. \- **Angle** : set the fold angle between the Zipper and the Pattern to express the fold . * **Particle Distance(mm)** \- Adjust Particle Distance for Zipper Tapes(ver4.1.0). * **Zipper Slider YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kuEU7A-rQzU ** * **Shape ** \- Choose the design of the Zipper slider. * **Size** \- Select the size of the Zipper slider from the provided presets, or type in a desired percentage to adjust manually. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Reverse Zipper Direction** option to locate the Zipper pull at either end of the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Move to Opposite Side** option to attach the Zipper pull to either half of the Zipper tape when the Zipper is unzipped. * **Material** \- Adjust provided options to add texture or colors to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express the Zipper slider as translucent or solid. **Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TsS-HVmHOE0 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D window. \- Right click on the Zipper tape/ slider to be edited. \- The pop-up menu with options below will appear. * **Zipper Tape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2HxuO5ZbOcI * **Delete** \- Delete the Zipper tape and slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Reverse (Right Clicked)** \- Similar to the Free Sewing tool, both halves of the Zipper tape need to be established in the same direction. If they are sewn incorrectly, the Zipper tape may twist. \- If Zipper appears to be deformed during Simulation, right-click and select **Reverse** to reverse the Sewing Line. * **Flip Normal (Right Clicked Teeth) ** \- Flip the fabric side of the Zipper tape in the 3D window. \- Select the Zipper Sewing Line, right-click and select **Flip Normal.** * **Deactivate/Freeze** \- Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper tape to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper seam line, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** \- To Reactivate or Unfreeze the deactivated/frozen Zipper tape, right-click the Zipper seam line again and select **Reactivate** or **Unfreeze.** * **Zipper Slider YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2az-u9u1ImQ** * **Delete -**Delete the Zipper Tape and Slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Deactivate/Freeze ****-** Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper Pull to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper Slider, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, editing, and managing zippers in 3D design software, complete with instructional videos and detailed steps for each process.

title: Userpool Settings
content: ## **New in 2024.2** #### **List of Contents** Concept Instruction FAQ #### **Concept** #### **What is Userpool?** A Userpool is a list of Members authorized to use the Owner's license. The license Owner can add or delete Members' email(CLO-SET account) who are allowed to use the license. Once the Member is added to the Userpool, Members can sign in to the software using their own CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. By doing so, the Owner no longer needs to share the license ID and password, enhancing security and collaboration efficiency. #### **Who can use Userpool?** Any users with the licenses to sign in to CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2 and later versions. #### **Where is Userpool provided?** The Userpool and a more detailed manual are provided in License Account Admin. Below is how you can access to the Userpool Settings page. Sign in clo3d.com > Click Account( ![account_icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712495769) ) on the top right side > Sign in ![License account admin.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720137497) > Click ![Userpool Setting.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720141849) on the left side #### **** #### **Instruction** #### **How to ADD members to the Userpool** **From the Userpool Settings** Click ![Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712513433) and type the Member's email address. For better management, you can set a Member name when adding a member. The Member will receive an invitation email with the software installer included. **From the Software (Auto Add)** If the CLO-SET account is signed in from the software, the account will be automatically added as a Member to the Userpool list. The Owner will receive the notification email when the new Member is auto added. If the Owner doesn't want the Members to be auto added, Auto Add option can be turned off. #### #### **How to DELETE members from the Userpool** Mark the Members from the list > Click ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39109913714841) Deleted Members cannot sign in to the software with their CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. Deleted Members can be added again whenever it's needed. #### **** #### **FAQ** **Can the license Owner be the Member of the other Userpool?** Yes. If the Owner's email has the CLO-SET account and that same account is invited to another Userpool, the account can also be a Member under another Userpool. **I am invited as a Userpool Member, but cannot sign in to the software.** The Member needs to be signed up to CLO-SET and have a CLO-SET account to sign in to the software. However, any email can be added when the Owner invites the Members. **Do the Userpool Owner and Member related to the CLO-SET group's admin and users(collaborator, editor, viewer)?** No, the Userpool is a separate feature from CLO-SET group permissions.
content_description: Discover how to efficiently manage access to your software licenses with the Userpool feature in CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2, enhancing security and collaboration among authorized members.

title: Fold/Sew Pleats
content: **Objective** Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats Fold** / **Pleats Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001057348/________.png)**Pleats Fold** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001012867/________.png)**Pleats Sewing** ** Operation** **Pleats Fold** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. → Pleats Fold window appears. 3. Select a desired type of pleats. → Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. **※****Note:** Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) 4. Check the **Reverse Direction** option as needed. **→** The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. 5. Click **OK** button to complete. **Pleats Sewing** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. ※**Note:** In case of sewing the pleat pattern only, press enter to proceed to the next step. (ver 6.0) 3. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. → Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). 4. Click on the end point to complete. → The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating, folding, and sewing various types of pleats in a 2D pattern design software.

title: Graphic Grouping
content: **List of Contents** Create a Graphic Group Add Sub-Graphics to a Group Select Graphics in a Group Show/Hide Graphics in a Group Ungroup **** ### **Objective** Group multiple graphics to organize and manage them as a unit in the 2D/3D window and Object Browser. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59496876602905)** #### **Create a Graphic Group** **Location** Object Browser ▶ Graphic Tab **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59496876602905)** **Operation** 1. Go to **Object Browser ▶ Graphic Tab**. 2. Hover over an existing graphic style and click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59496876603033) button that appears on the right. → A Graphic Group is created, with the existing graphic added as the first sub-style. → A file dialog opens to select an additional graphic file. 3. Select a graphic file. → The selected graphic is added as the second sub-style within the group. → The group is named **Graphic_StyleGroup_[ID]** by default. 4. To rename the group, right-click the group header and select **Rename**. **※ Note:** Sub-styles within a Graphic Group cannot be used to create standalone graphics. **** ### **Add Sub-Graphics to a Group** 1. Go to **Object Browser ▶ Graphic Tab** and expand the Graphic Group. 2. Click the **+** button on the group header row. → A file dialog opens. 3. Select a graphic file. → The graphic is added as a new sub-style within the group. **** ### **Select Graphics in a Group** 1. Activate **Transform Graphic** from the 2D/3D Toolbar. 2. Click on a grouped graphic in the 2D/3D window. → The entire Graphic Group is selected. → The Property Editor shows **Group Configuration** (Face, Over Seamline, Fur Trimmer) and **Group Transformation** (Angle, Z-Offset). 3. Double-click on an individual graphic within the group. → The individual sub-graphic is selected. → The Property Editor shows **Graphic Configuration** (Face, Over Seamline, Fur Trimmer), **Graphic Transformation** (Lock Graphic, Angle, Z-Offset), **Link All Colorways** , and **2D Measurements** (To Center, To Outline). **** ### **Show/Hide Graphics in a Group** 1. Go to **Object Browser ▶ Graphic Tab** and expand the Graphic Group. 2. Hover over a sub-style and click the visibility icon to show or hide it. → The visibility state is applied to the corresponding graphic in the 2D/3D window. → The Show/Hide setting is reflected across Colorways. **** ### **Ungroup** 1. Go to **Object Browser ▶ Graphic Tab**. 2. Right-click the Graphic Group header and select **Ungroup**. → The group is dissolved and all sub-styles become individual graphic styles. → Any graphics in the 2D/3D window that referenced the group are also ungrouped. **※ Note:** Other options available in the right-click menu: **Delete** , **Delete All Unused Graphics** , **Rename** , **Reset**.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for organizing and managing graphics in groups within the 2D/3D window and Object Browser.

title: Reverse Arrangement Horizontally/Vertically
content: ### **Objective** Flip 3D Garment Patterns horizontally and vertically while maintaining its curvature. **※ Note:** Flipping Patterns while maintaining its curvature is only applicable for patterns arranged with [Arrangement Points](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001999287). **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005703927/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** ▶ 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reverse-Arrange ▶ **Horizontally** / **Vertically** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005703927/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** ▶ 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reverse-Arrange ▶ **Horizontally** / **Vertically** → The selected Pattern is now being flipped over horizontally/vertically while maintaining its curvature.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for flipping 3D garment patterns both horizontally and vertically while preserving their curvature, specifically for patterns arranged with Arrangement Points.

title: I get an error message saying, "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found." How should I solve the problem?
content: **Question** I get an error message saying "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found." How should I solve the problem? **Answer** This issue often occurs when the program cannot find the dongle key for authentication. Please refer to the [manual](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) to learn how to solve the issue in detail.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on resolving the "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found" error by explaining the authentication dongle key issue and directing users to the relevant manual for detailed instructions.

title: Segment Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Segment Sewing Establish Sewing Lines Directional Notches Divide Sewing Lines Based on Notches **Segment Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xlE08VVux5M \- Establish Sewing Lines on segments, split by points, to connect Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing.** ** Establish Sewing Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxXoWyYlINc \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on a segment on a Pattern to establish the first half of the Sewing Line. \- Then, hover the mouse over the segment where the second half of the Sewing Line will be placed to. \- Drag the mouse to alter the direction of the Directional Notch as desired. \- Click on the segment to establish the second half of the Sewing Line. \- A pair of Sewing Lines is completed. \- The Sewing Line difference will hover over the mouse cursor. \- When the Sewing Line difference is larger than 1mm, the value will appear in red to alert users. **Directional Notches** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6RfaA1mApNk \- The direction of the Directional Notches can be changed by moving the mouse on the Sewing Lines. \- To reset the Directional Notches on a pair of Sewing Lines, hit the ESC key or the Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard. **Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches(ver4.1.0)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jvyaHp-R5c0 \- Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png)**Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Establish sewing lines based on notches. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance on using segment sewing techniques, including establishing sewing lines, adjusting directional notches, and dividing sewing lines based on notches, complemented by instructional YouTube videos.
